pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptor (Anti-NMDAR) Encephalitis THE SMOKING GUN: A targeted pelvic MRI revealed a 3.5 cm mature cystic ovarian teratoma containing ectopic, dysplastic neural tissue. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Ectopic neural tissue within the ovarian teratoma expresses functional NMDA receptors. The patient's immune system recognizes these neuronal elements as foreign, producing pathogenic IgG autoantibodies against the GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor. These autoantibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and bind to glutamate receptors in the brain, causing cross-linking and internalisation of NMDARs. The loss of NMDAR-mediated synaptic function—particularly on cortical GABAergic interneurons—causes massive forebrain disinhibition, producing the classic progression from acute psychosis to dyskinesias, catatonia, autonomic collapse, and hypoventilation.
